implement: legion-worker: the phase contract this issue runs under - the shared workspace, the handoff, the push rules and the pull request the implementer opens.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the implementer writes the pull request body and its E2E line, and this change's only proof surface is a CI run id, which that reference defines the shape of.

legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md: the change deletes code and a documented control (use-show-activity.ts, both localStorage keys, the Show activity, Show retracted and Resolved (N) controls, the event rows in the Conversation), and this reference is how a deletion is carried through its callers, tests and docs.
ce-simplify-code: ConversationTab.tsx (1609 lines) and conversation-model.ts (639) are rewritten, so the simplify pass over the settled result is part of the implementation, not an afterthought.
dispatch-first and dispatch: every message, comment or ask the implementer posts on INFRA-44 goes through the dispatch command, and dispatch-first is loaded in every session that has Dispatch.
test: legion-worker: the tester's phase contract, its verdict and its handoff.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: it defines what a proof is (the changed behaviour on a production-like surface with its command or run id, what was observed, the head sha and a negative control) and states that the tester reads CI for everything static rather than re-running it - which is the whole of this change's static evidence, since neither the Playwright suite nor the Go server tests can run in a Legion pod.
dispatch-first and dispatch: loaded in every Dispatch session; the tester writes nothing to Dispatch except through those commands.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's phase contract and the order of a review round.

legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the order of the gate, the reviewer's submission and the approved head READY is compared against - and this change's two proving CI jobs (dispatch, envoy-go) are not required checks, so refusing a red head is the reviewer's own act, not the gate's.
legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: one disposition reply per thread and the bot findings the reviewer accepts, for a pull request this size.
dispatch-first and dispatch: loaded in every Dispatch session; the reviewer's writes to INFRA-44 go through those commands.

findings.finding: F1 - Conversation cards built from the comments and asks routes lose the event id and seq that pinning (pinned_items:event:<id> in user_issue_state.dismissed), the dwell read mark (data-event-seq) and Jump to latest are all keyed on; only an ask carries an event id (opened_event_id).
findings.answer: The plan gives a conversation its own pin identity: pins.ts gains conversationItemId({kind,id}) producing ask:<id>/comment:<id>/message:<id> and pinnedConversationIds beside today's pinnedEventIds; a Conversation card pins with the conversation marker, an Activity row keeps the event marker, and the margin's Pinned tab resolves both. No migration: a conversation pinned before the change keeps rendering in the margin as its event line while its card shows unpinned until re-pinned, which the pull request body states. The read mark and Jump to latest stop needing a per-card seq (see F3).

findings.finding: F2 - 'Newest reply first' has no sort key for an ask: listIssueAsks discards the last-reply map queryOwnerAsks computes (api/asks.go:674) and there is no answered_at column; the answer's time is inside the answer JSON.
findings.answer: The plan adds last_reply and thread to each row of GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks, as a row struct embedding model.Ask so the JSON stays a superset, reusing loadInboxAskThreads (api/inbox_queries.go:88). A conversation's sort key is the newest of its root's created_at, its newest reply's created_at and, for an ask, answer.at and resolution.at; an edit does not move it; ties break on id. Recorded as spec departure 2.

findings.finding: F3 - 'By the read mark the issue already keeps' names two mechanisms: user_issue_state.last_read_seq (an events seq) and user_threads (rows only for threads the reader wrote in, open asks deliberately excluded).
findings.answer: The plan uses last_read_seq, the only one that is the issue's own, and converts it to a time with one event read (?after=<last_read_seq>&order=asc&limit=1): a conversation is unread when its newest activity is at or after that boundary, and Jump to latest reads N new over unread conversations. A second one-row read (?order=desc&limit=1) gives the head seq the dwell on the newest conversation writes back; dwelling lower writes nothing, since a watermark cannot express per-conversation read state and under-marking never hides an unread conversation. Only the Conversation writes the mark; Activity renders it and writes nothing. Named in the completion summary for the architect, who may overrule.

findings.finding: F4 - The Activity tab's own behaviour is entirely unspecified: pagination, live append, unread divider, Jump to latest, read-mark writing, pinning.
findings.answer: The plan settles each: Activity is today's event rendering moved, keeping the useInfiniteQuery over ['events', key] (200 per page, desc), Load older, day dividers, the unread divider read from last_read_seq, and event pinning; it has no composer, no filters and writes no read mark, so the watermark has one writer. Its list carries aria-label='Issue activity' so a test can tell the two lists apart.

findings.finding: F5 - dispatch://KEY/log already means the issue's event list to every agent (dispatch-execute.ts:3494-3498) while criterion 1 requires it keep opening the Conversation in a browser, so one spelling means two things.
findings.answer: The plan changes no agent behaviour: /log keeps reading the event list, /conversation keeps normalising to /log, and 'activity' is accepted as a spelling of the existing log kind so dispatch://KEY/activity reads the event list the Activity tab shows. The residual divergence is reported to the architect as a decision it may want in the spec, since re-pointing the agent side changes what every running agent reads.

findings.finding: F6 - No parser accepts dispatch://KEY/activity, and DISPATCH_HREF_REFERENCES is a four-package contract tested against three parsers; the Go extractor accepts neither log nor conversation, so such a reference would create no backlink.
findings.answer: The plan makes activity first-class in the SPA grammar (parseIssueReference, parseIssuePath, buildIssuePath, buildDispatchReference, shortForm, issueTabForRoute, referenceRouteFromHref) and in the agent parser, and deliberately leaves text/refs.go and dispatch-href.ts alone, so the reference renders as a link and creates no backlink - exactly today's dispatch://KEY/log. Recorded as spec departure 3 so criterion 1 is read as parity, not as indexing.

findings.finding: F7 - Criterion 2's 'lands on it, marked' does not say what is marked, and an ask's replies are drawn by a shared AskCard/AskThread with no per-reply marking; a landing on a conversation the current filter excludes is also unaddressed.
findings.answer: The plan marks both: the conversation's li keeps aria-current='true' and data-turn='<kind>:<id>' as every landing asserts today, and when the link names a reply that reply's row is marked too - comment and message replies already carry aria-current, and AskCard/AskThread gain one optional currentReplyId prop that only the Conversation passes, which also opens the collapsed thread. A landing resets the filter to All, so a link never fails to land.

findings.finding: F8 - Which turn kinds are conversations, and each one's Open/Closed bucket, is unstated for targeted messages, delivery rows and a root comment with no replies.
findings.answer: The plan enumerates them: an ask is one card, Open while state is open and Closed once answered or resolved (retracted included); a comment thread is one card per root comment including one with no replies, Closed once resolved or its suggestion is accepted or rejected; a message thread is one card per root message, targeted or not, never closed and listed under All and Open, keeping today's TargetedMessageCard rendering as one card; every delivery, acceptance and lifecycle event is Activity only, with delivery state folding into its card as today.

findings.finding: F9 - A fifth tab no longer fits a 390 px phone on one line (Tabs.tsx), and two e2e specs assert that four do.
findings.answer: The plan accepts the sideways scroll at 390 px, keeps every tab reachable and the 44 px touch targets, and rewrites both the Tabs.tsx comment and the artifacts.e2e.ts assertion with the AGENTS.md note. Recorded as spec departure 4 and raised to the architect, since shortening a label is the alternative and changes what the human approved.

findings.finding: F10 - 'Not carried over from an earlier visit' is satisfiable by component state, a URL parameter or stored-and-ignored, with different costs.
findings.answer: Plain useState with 'all' as the initial value: a URL parameter would become part of the route grammar and of every copied link, which nothing asks for. use-show-activity.ts and both of its localStorage keys are deleted outright, so a browser that still carries them is one the code never consults.

findings.finding: F11 - 'The Resolved (N) controls go' does not say which: the Conversation has one and the margin's ThreadList has another, and the issue's non-goal is that the margin is unchanged.
findings.answer: Only the Conversation's goes; the margin keeps its Resolved (N) and its retracted fold. The two e2e cases that live in margin-named files but click the Conversation's control (threads.e2e.ts:291-293, margin.e2e.ts:385-387) are rewritten, and the margin suites pass with their margin assertions unmodified, which is the plan's acceptance row for 'the review margin is unchanged'.

findings.finding: F12 - Criterion 1 requires a keyboard shortcut of its own but names none, and t a is already Artifacts; the chord help list is asserted.
findings.answer: t v, because t a is Artifacts and l is already an issue-scope single-key binding. activatedTabs gains its entry, the ? help list gains its row, IssuePageFallback's hardcoded label list gains Activity, and keyboard-issue.e2e.ts and AGENTS.md:192 are rewritten together.

findings.finding: F13 - Liveness is keyed on the ['events', key] query and the ask/comment detail keys; moving cards off events would silently un-live the tab, and a card can change bucket while the reader watches.
findings.answer: Three new keys, ['issue-asks', key], ['issue-comments', key], ['issue-messages', key], added to api/sse.ts's event-to-key map so every ask.*, comment.*, suggestion.* and message.* event invalidates the owning list; prependEventToLog keeps serving Activity's ['events', key] pages. A card changing bucket live is allowed, not frozen. __tests__/sse.test.ts is rewritten with the map.

findings.finding: F14 - The view link now points off its own tab, and most Activity lines have no link at all.
findings.answer: The view link on a comment.created line keeps pointing at /issues/<KEY>/comments/<id>, which now lands on the Conversation with the conversation and the reply marked. No other event kind gains a link: nothing asks for it and each is its own design question.

findings.finding: F15 - Criteria 1, 2, 4 and 5 are not machine-checkable as written, and /issues/K/log is not even a SPA path (parseIssuePath returns undefined for it).
findings.answer: The plan's Acceptance table adopts the restatements: the seeded 5-conversation issue drawing exactly 5 li[data-turn] and 0 [data-kind=activity] with at least 3 rows on /activity; one marked li and one marked reply row per landing case; the named margin suites passing unmodified; a routes.test.ts table asserting parseDispatchReference('dispatch://K/log') and parseIssuePath('/issues/K/conversation') both resolve to the conversation route (the path /issues/K/log is not claimed anywhere); and the dispatch CI run as criterion 5's artifact.

findings.finding: F16 - Criterion 5 requires proof on the running application, but the Playwright suite cannot run in a Legion worker pod and the only surface that runs it, CI's dispatch job, is not a required check.
findings.answer: The plan names the inner loop that does run in the pod (biome, tsc, bun test web/src, go build and go vet) and makes the production-like surface the CI jobs dispatch and envoy-go, cited by run URL and head sha, with reading both runs an explicit tester and reviewer obligation since neither is required. The architect is told the suite cannot run in a pod and that making the job required or funding a pgvector Postgres for pods are the two human-only alternatives.

findings.finding: F17 - Inventory of the e2e specs and component tests that encode today's behaviour, plus the blast radius of IssueRoute/IssueTab/buildIssuePath/parseIssuePath and the search route's own /comments/<id> deep link.
findings.answer: The plan carries that inventory verbatim as its 'Tests that assert today's behaviour' section, each entry rewritten to the new behaviour or deleted with its reason (including keyboard-issue.e2e.ts:599-620, whose rule needs another page-level checkbox to stay provable), names every exhaustive consumer of the route union in its work order, and adds the search hit to the landing acceptance row.

findings.finding: F18 - Claims in the spec that the code does not support: (c) the server lists comments and asks 'whatever state they are in' reads as though no server work is implied; (f) Resolved (N) is not a stored setting; (e) removing event lines removes the only place an event can be pinned from; (d) dispatch://KEY/log has never been indexed by the Go extractor.
findings.answer: The plan's 'Corrections to the spec's description of today's code' section records (c), (f) and (e) for the architect to fold in, and the plan already builds to the corrected facts: the server work is declared as departures 1 and 2, nothing is claimed about stored Resolved state, and event pinning moves to the Activity tab while a conversation gets its own pin identity. (d) is qualified by departure 3, which states that an activity reference renders as a link and creates no backlink, at parity with /log.

specDepartures.spec: The server 'lists no message threads, so those come from the event history, which the tab reads 200 events at a time'.
specDepartures.plan: A new route, GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/messages, returns every root message of the issue with its replies and delivery attempts, unpaged, mirroring /comments; the event history is no longer a source of conversation cards.
specDepartures.evidence: routes_table.go:95-97 mounts only POST, GET /issues/{key}/messages/{id} and GET /messages/{id}, and ConversationTab.tsx:866-871 reads events 200 at a time, so a message thread older than the loaded window is absent - which the spec's own check (a conversation older than 200 events listed without the reader asking for older history) forbids. listAgentMessages (api/messages.go:542-650) already composes loadMessageReplyChains and loadMessageDeliveries, so the per-issue query is the simpler half of one that exists.

outcome.scope: One new Go handler, one row in api/routes_table.go with the pinned count in routes_table_test.go, its Go tests and one client method, none of which the spec's sentence anticipates.

specDepartures.spec: 'The Dispatch server already lists an issue's comments and its asks whatever state they are in', which reads as though the Conversation needs no server change.
specDepartures.plan: GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks additionally carries each ask's last_reply and its thread, as a row struct embedding model.Ask so the JSON stays a superset of today's.
specDepartures.evidence: listIssueAsks discards the last-reply map queryOwnerAsks already computes (api/asks.go:674, api/ask_rows.go:32-35) and there is no answered_at column (model.AskAnswer, model/model.go:886), so 'newest reply first' has no sort key for an ask. The thread also removes the per-card GET /asks/{id} the spec itself flags (useAskAnswerForm.ts:124-130, staleTime Infinity, nothing batching), reusing the Inbox's own loadInboxAskThreads (api/inbox_queries.go:88).

outcome.scope: One Go handler change and its tests, plus the client types, in a package the spec implies is untouched.

specDepartures.spec: The Activity tab is 'written dispatch://KEY/activity in a reference'.
specDepartures.plan: activity is a first-class reference in the dashboard's grammar and in the agent client, and is deliberately not added to the Go reference extractor or to the shared href table, so such a reference renders as a link and creates no backlink.
specDepartures.evidence: internal/dispatch/text/refs.go:151-205 accepts for an issue only the bare key, spec, artifact/<slug> and (ask|comment|message)/<id> - neither log nor conversation - so dispatch://KEY/log is not indexed today either; packages/contracts/src/dispatch-href.ts has no conversation or log row and is one table three parsers are tested against, so a row is a four-package contract change nothing in the issue requires.

acceptance: Criterion 1's 'written dispatch://KEY/activity in a reference' is met at parity with dispatch://KEY/log: the dashboard links it and no backlink or ReferencedBy row is created.

specDepartures.spec: Criterion 4 lists 'the note about four tabs fitting a 390 px phone' in packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md among the passages to rewrite, treating it as documentation.
specDepartures.plan: The plan accepts that the issue tablist scrolls sideways at 390 px with five tabs, keeps every tab reachable and the 44 px touch targets, and rewrites the Tabs.tsx comment and the e2e assertion alongside the note.
specDepartures.evidence: components/Tabs.tsx:97-100 states four compact tabs fit 390 px on one line and that at 360 px the tablist scrolls; e2e/artifacts.e2e.ts:236-255 asserts exactly four tabs with per-tab geometry at the iPhone width, so the note is asserted behaviour and a fifth tab changes what a phone reader sees.

acceptance: A phone reader scrolls the issue tablist sideways to reach the last tab, where four tabs fit on one line before this change.
